I found the most fascinating divergence in global macro.

The most recent South Korean consumer sentiment reading sits above 100, meaning optimists outnumber pessimists, and has held near multi-year highs. 

Meanwhile U.S. consumer sentiment is at its lowest on record. 

So why does one country feel rich and the other feel broke? Both countries saw their stock markets rip to record highs this year. 

The KOSPI is up 57% compared to the S&P at just 9.5% YTD, that could explain it. But it's not necessarily the returns that create the divergence.

It's HOW citizens in each country own stocks.

Korea has 105 million active brokerage accounts in a country of 51 million people. Retail is roughly half of all trading volume. Margin debt just hit an all time high of 38.5 trillion won. Samsung and SK Hynix alone account for 51% of daily market turnover, and once you add the single stock leverage and inverse ETFs, it clears 80%.

Koreans don't have "exposure" to the market. They ARE the market. Direct, concentrated, levered. The KOSPI doubled in 9 months and every kitchen table in Seoul FELT it. That's your consumer sentiment print.

America is the opposite. 58% of families own stock but only 21% picked individual stocks, and that ownership number has been flat near 20% for three decades. The percentage of Americans trying to make multi-bagger returns is a tiny fraction of Koreans. 

Because of this, Americans have exposure to the markets but don't really feel it. They glance at a quarterly 401k statement moving up with the index and go back to paying for gas. They're not building an active trading strategy around thematics or speculating on AI bottlenecks.

Fable 5 tells me only about half of Americans might recognize Nvidia by name, even less could tell you what it does. Meanwhile, 99% of Korean people know their largest companies like Samsung and SK Hynix intimatley.

Of course, it's likely that the next consumer sentiment reading in Korea will be markedly lower after the country's stock market has fallen 20% in just the last month. Leverage, speculation, and active trading around a couple of companies is a two way street.

But certainly a fascinating difference between two economies at the center of the AI revolution.

A lot of people on X are new to the markets. So I'll make this as simple and harsh as possible.

The economy is not going up. It is not going down. It is doing both at the same time. This is called a "K-shaped
economy" and almost nobody talking about affordability on your timeline understands what it actually means.

If you own assets, stocks and real estate, you are on the upper arm of the K. Your wealth has compounded aggressively since 2020. The S&P is at all-time highs. Home prices are up 50% since the pandemic. Your 401k is the best it has ever been.

If you do NOT own assets, you are on the lower arm. Rent is higher. Groceries cost more. A home that cost 2.2x the median income in 1960 now costs 5 to 7x. You are working harder and falling further behind, and it is not your imagination.

The top 10% of Americans own 93% of all stocks. The bottom 50% own 1%. The top 10% hold 68% of total wealth. The bottom 50% hold 2.5%. This is not an opinion. This is Federal Reserve data.

When the S&P goes up 25% in a year, the people who own stocks get 25% wealthier. The people who don't own stocks get nothing. That is the K. Same economy.

The last time wealth concentration looked like this was the Gilded Age, 1870 to 1900. That lasted 30 years before structural reform changed anything.

What does this mean for you? 
The K-shaped economy is not a reason to panic. It is a reason to understand where you sit and what you can control. 

The people on the upper arm did not get lucky. They owned assets. That is the entire difference.

Change your life and start small. No matter how small your account balance is. I only started with $10K, twenty years ago. This is your time to retire your whole family. They are counting on you.

本周 VIX 回到 14-15，大家可能觉得波动率没什么好说的了。但如果回头看 7 月中旬到 8 月中旬这一个月，个股端经历的不是普通的“财报后 IV crush”，而是一次极端拥挤的 dispersion 结构反向收敛。理解这件事对接下来怎么做期权至关重要。

初始条件：极端的个股高 IV / 指数低 IV 错位

7 月中旬，Cboe 的 DSPX（dispersion 指数）升到约 50%，创六年高位。与此同时 VIX 只有约 15。hyperscaler 个股 IV 约 40%，SPY 前端 IV 只有约 10%。COR1M（1 个月相关性）处于极低水平。

这个错位是怎么来的？三层溢价叠在一起：①财报风险溢价，大科技股财报集中落地前，零售开仓中 call buying 占比 56%（接近年内最高），主动买权推高事件方差；②AI 内部剧烈分化，半导体，软件，大型云各走各的，极低的股票相关性让指数 IV 没有同步上升；③7 月 momentum unwind 的尾部风险溢价，7 月科技股经历历史级别的动量平仓，单名股 realized vol 被连续大涨大跌抬高。

我们知道，指数方差 = 个股权重平方*个股方差之和 + 跨项相关系数。个股波动率很高，但隐含相关性极低，所以 VIX 可以很低。这个结构本身就是一个交易，买个股 vol、卖指数 vol、押注股票继续各走各的。这个交易在 2024-2026 年已经变得极度拥挤。

8 月初开始，四个力量同时作用于这个拥挤结构：

第一推动力：财报事件方差集中退出。 Microsoft、Google、Amazon、Meta、Apple 财报陆续落地。财报一出，事件方差几乎立刻消失。Cboe 在 8/3 就观察到 VIX 一周降 2.6 点但 VIXEQ 降 3.4 点，个股端跌得更快。但这只是触发器。普通财报季每季度都有，这次之所以这么猛，是因为财报前 DSPX 已经在六年极值。

第二推动力：拥挤的 dispersion 被反向平仓，这是最重要的放大器。 此前主流 dispersion 交易是买个股 vol / 卖指数 vol。QVR 等波动率基金甚至已经转向 reverse dispersion（买指数 vol / 卖 single-name vol），因为单名股 IV 与指数 IV 的差已经到了极端水平。财报落地后，长个股 vol 的一方同时面临：事件方差消失、theta 流失、VIXEQ/DSPX 跌破趋势、止损触发。reverse-dispersion 交易者同时在卖个股 IV。这不是自然衰减，是一轮仓位反转，这解释了为什么没有财报、或财报已经过去的股票，IV 也一起遭到压缩。市场卖的不是单个事件，是整个 single-name vol asset class。

第三推动力：7 月去杠杆结束，regime 从“怕个股爆炸”切换到“怕踏空上涨”。7 月发生历史级别科技 momentum unwind，相当一部分杠杆已被清理，去杠杆完成后市场反而具备更高质量反弹的条件。随后是典型的 underexposed chase，SPX 在截至 8/4 的四个交易日涨 5.8%，7 月 30 日至 8 月 5 日成为历史上 SPX call 成交量最高的五日窗口，短期 call skew 升至两年高位。

第四推动力：系统资金 releveraging 的负反馈循环。 截至 8/10，SOX 前十大成分股的平均 3 个月 ATM IV 仅 8 月以来就降了近 20 %。低波动率允许系统策略重新增加敞口 -> 加仓推高股价 -> 上涨进一步压低下行波动率需求 -> 更低的波动率又释放更多系统资金购买能力。这是一轮典型的 vol-control 反馈：IV 下降 -> 预期风险下降 -> 系统资金加仓 -> 股价趋势改善 -> RV 下降 -> IV 进一步下降。

这轮 crush需要让我们意识到方向正确 ≠ call 赚钱

整体 ATM IV 可以暴跌，同时远端 OTM call 仍然变贵。call demand 很强不代表你持有的 ATM 或轻度 OTM call 不会被 IV crush。Cboe 发现 8/10 前后 SPX skew 降至一年低位，但 deep OTM puts 仍有需求——这是波动率曲面的重新定价，不是所有期权都没人买。

这解释了为什么在这种环境里“方向正确”不等于“call 赚钱”。即使方向判断正确，IV 下跌带来的 Vega 损失与 Theta 损耗，仍然可能吃掉全部 Delta 收益。当 IV 变化大幅为负时，即使方向对了，总收益也可能是负的。

这轮 crush 本质上更像一次投机杠杆清洗后的波动率正常化。7 月动量股回撤、杠杆 AI 产品清算、单名股期权仓位去化之后：短期期权需求下降、散户和动量资金减少追涨、个股 realized vol 回落、Dealer 不再需要持续追着 spot 做 gamma hedge、单名股 IV 系统性下压。

现在的特殊之处在于期权结构的错位：single name stock的 ATM IV 相对便宜，但 25 Delta 和 10 Delta wings 仍然贵。 指数和个股的 term structure 都已经降到偏低区间。这对期权结构的含义很明确：想赌方向，ATM 附近的 call spread 仍然合理；想赌 IV 回归，优先买 ATM 或轻度 OTM 单腿期权吃最大 vega；不适合为了“便宜”去买很远的 wing，因为 wing skew 反而没有同步 crush。买的是被 crush 得最厉害的 ATM/轻度 OTM vol，而不是仍然昂贵的deep OTM put/call。

crush 是否已经结束？

截至 8/14：VIX 约 14.25，DSPX 约 33.45，SPY IV 处于过去一年第 4 百分位。但中位数个股 IV 仍在第 31 百分位，个股 realized volatility 仍在第 61 百分位——implied dispersion 已经下降，但 realized dispersion 尚未明显下降。IV 可能开始跑在 RV 前面。

接下来两种情景：

如果个股实际波动也逐渐下降，IV crush 还能慢慢延续。如果 realized dispersion 继续高，当前低 IV 会重新吸引买盘。此外 8/19 VIX 到期和 8/21 月度 OPEX 会移除部分压制指数波动率的 gamma 仓位，而 NVDA 财报、Jackson Hole 等事件紧接着到来。届时如果相关性开始上升，修复路径可能从“个股 IV 下跌”切换成“指数 IV 上涨”。

The Shiller CAPE ratio is at 42.2x. The only time it was higher in 154 years was the dot-com bubble at 43.8x.

But here's the thing most people get wrong: the CAPE can stay elevated for years. It crossed 25x in 1996 and didn't peak until 2000.

What the CAPE actually tells you is not WHEN to sell. It tells you WHAT your forward returns will look like. When CAPE is above 40x, the S&P 500 has averaged +2.3% annually over the next 10 years. When it's below 15x, it averaged +10.7%.

You don't have to sell. But you should know what you're buying into.

The CAPE ratio measures how expensive the stock market is relative to the last 10 years of inflation adjusted earnings. Think of it as a price tag on the entire market. The higher the number, the more you're paying for each dollar of earnings.
